evidence.quote: I would say that an expectation of higher near-term policy rates does not appear to be causing the increase in longer-term rates.
An unexpected sharp increase in rates could lead to heightened volatility in financial markets, stresses to market liquidity, and downward pressures for asset prices.
The household sector, taken as a whole, looks quite resilient.
In conclusion, the financial system is substantially more resilient than it was in the mid-2000s.

parsed.rationale: This is a financial stability speech that takes no explicit monetary policy view; its only policy-adjacent remark notes that markets are not pricing higher near-term policy rates. Its emphasis on downside financial risks from higher rates gives a slight dovish tilt.
